description: HPO terms for the 20 blau checklist items (configs/checklists/blau.json), chosen on 2026-11-15 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-40 as extended by D-47. 'observed' is the one term a record may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite no single term covers exactly (the free-text feature rows carry the specific term). 'excluded' lists every term a record may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

granulomatous dermatitis or skin rash.note: Composite: Skin rash and Cutaneous granuloma (HPO has no 'granulomatous dermatitis' term); neither is an ancestor of the other, and their nearest shared ancestors (Granuloma, Inflammatory abnormality of the skin) are each broader than the item.

arthritis or joint synovitis.note: Composite: Arthritis (EXACT 'Joint inflammation') and Synovitis (child Granulomatous synovitis); in HPO Synovitis sits under Abnormal synovial membrane morphology, not under Arthritis, and neither is an ancestor of the other. Tenosynovitis is not under either, so excluding them does not exclude item 3.

tenosynovitis.note: Tenosynovitis; exact name match (Digital flexor tenosynovitis is a descendant).

camptodactyly.note: Camptodactyly; exact name match (camptodactyly of finger and of toe are descendants).

uveitis.note: Uveitis; exact name match. Granulomatous, anterior, posterior and panuveitis are descendants, and Iridocyclitis is a descendant through Anterior uveitis.

glaucoma or raised intraocular pressure.note: Composite: Glaucoma and Ocular hypertension (EXACT 'Raised intraocular pressure', 'Increased intraocular pressure'); neither is an ancestor of the other, and Abnormal intraocular pressure would include low pressure, so it is broader.

visual impairment or blindness.note: Visual impairment; exact name match. Blindness (through Reduced visual acuity) and Visual loss are descendants, so the one term covers both parts.

fever.note: Fever; exact name match (recurrent and persistent fever are descendants).

erythema nodosum or panniculitis.note: Composite: Erythema nodosum and Panniculitis; in HPO Erythema nodosum is not under Panniculitis (its parent is Inflammatory abnormality of the skin, which is broader than the item), so no single term covers both.

lymphadenopathy.note: Lymphadenopathy; exact name match (Granulomatous and Generalized lymphadenopathy are descendants).

hepatomegaly or hepatic granulomas.note: Hepatomegaly. HPO has no hepatic or liver granuloma term (searched 'hepatic granuloma', 'liver granuloma', 'granulomatous'); Granuloma is broader than the item, so observed is null and only the hepatomegaly component can be excluded.

splenomegaly.note: Splenomegaly; exact name match (Hepatosplenomegaly is a descendant).

vasculitis (large-vessel arteritis, aort.note: Vasculitis; the parenthetical is read as the forms the reviews name. Large vessel vasculitis and Leukocytoclastic vasculitis are descendants of Vasculitis; Arteritis and Aortitis are not (they sit under arterial and aortic morphology), so they are excluded separately. Asserting Vasculitis for a reported aortitis or arteritis is clinically correct even though HPO files them elsewhere.

systemic hypertension.note: Hypertension (EXACT 'Systemic hypertension', 'Arterial hypertension'); pulmonary and ocular hypertension are separate terms, not descendants.

interstitial lung disease.note: Abnormal pulmonary interstitial morphology (EXACT 'Interstitial lung disease'); Interstitial pneumonitis, Pulmonary fibrosis and Pulmonary granulomatosis are descendants.

granulomatous nephritis or renal failure.note: Renal insufficiency (EXACT 'Renal failure'). HPO has no granulomatous nephritis term; Nephritis and Tubulointerstitial nephritis (EXACT 'Interstitial nephritis') are broader than granulomatous nephritis, so they are neither asserted nor excluded, and observed is null.

cranial or other neuropathy (facial pals.note: Composite: Cranial nerve paralysis (EXACT 'Cranial nerve palsy'; Facial palsy is a descendant) and Peripheral neuropathy (for the 'other' or transient neuropathies); neither is an ancestor of the other. HPO has no general 'neuropathy' or 'cranial neuropathy' term; Abnormality of the peripheral nervous system is broader (morphology, neoplasms).

elevated inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP).note: Composite: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and Elevated circulating C-reactive protein concentration. Their shared parent, Acute phase response, is broader (it includes ferritin, hepcidin, serum amyloid A and calcium-phosphate hormone terms), so observed is null.
